## Summary

He open-sourced **numbrone** (github.com/stevenmichaelthomas/numbrone — repo created 2026-11-08, ~99 stars in its first day): "a chief of staff for your coding agents," a community project built on herdr. Architecture:

- **Chief** — the one agent you talk to; does *not* write code; routes and delegates plain-language requests, tracks everything, watches inbound sources (Linear, GitHub issues, …).
- **Managers** — one per project, living in that project's herdr workspace; answers small things itself (questions, investigations), spawns workers for code changes, and reviews their work before reporting it ready.
- **Workers** — one per task, each in its own herdr tab **and its own git worktree** (branch `numbrone/<task>`), so many tasks run at once without stepping on each other or on your checkout. Reports flow back up: worker → manager → chief → you.

Implementation detail that matters: the whole system is **one skill + one bash script + three Markdown role files**, and all state is plain text files you can read and edit. Claimed throughput: **~50–100 PRs/day across several personal projects**; he calls the model "expressive and perfect for ADHD brains."

From the quoted tweet (context): he switched to this working model two weeks prior — "central context and interface and the ability to fan out to get work done; high-level context in one place, localized deeper context across additional agent trees," with herdr keeping large workloads structured "beyond tabs and split panes."

## Why it matters

- Independent validation of the org shape this vault already runs on (chief routes a board queue; per-domain agents own their lanes): numbrone is the same chief → manager → worker tree, credited with 50–100 PRs/day in a coding context. The design choices rhyme with what works here: the chief routes instead of doing; state is plain text (auditable, greppable); workers isolated in worktrees (no shared-checkout races).
- The counterweight is already in the vault: [[2026-10-24-calvingrunewald-minimize-human-attention]] — 9 months scaling parallel agents *with herdr* ended in "my brain was melting." Throughput wasn't his constraint; attention was. Numbrone's reporting spine (worker→manager→chief→you) is one answer, but Calvin's wall says even a clean hierarchy needs an attention budget.
- The "ADHD brains" framing echoes the [[2026-11-08-brian-armstrong-agent-org-queue]] thesis: agent orgs as attention prosthetics, not just automation — one interface, fan-out underneath.
- **Skepticism gates:** 50–100 PRs/day is a self-reported peak on the author's own projects; the repo is a day old (no evidence yet on maintenance, review quality, or what fraction of those PRs actually merge); macOS/Linux only (herdr requirement) — not directly runnable on the Windows host.
- Reference only — the pattern is the value; the stack here already implements it.
